newsitem.title: USA: Philip Morris split may help value - report.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris split may help value - report.

text.p: A breakup of Philip Morris Cos Inc into food and tobacco units may help shareholder value, Business Week's Inside Wall Street column said.

Philip Morris's board rejected the idea two years ago, but the company is reportedly studying all options to boost the value of its stock, which is trading at 97-3/8, the magazine said. The stock reached a high of 107-3/8 earlier this year.
A large investor told the magazine that splitting the tobacco operations and creating domestic and foreign tobacco units to be spun off to shareholders.

This move would help define the value of Kraft Foods and its brewing business that features Miller Beer, as well as the fast growing international tobacco business and the hugely profitable U.S. tobacco unit, the magazine said.
A spokesman declined to comment to the magazine on speculation that a break up of the company is being considered. A Philip Morris representative was not immediately available for comment.
